annotations.text:
CLICKABLE — bet → sign → answer → breakdown. "Next turn" resets it.

Use the DOMAIN chip above the frame to switch between the five sign types. Each is a different physical object with its own item, question, breakdown and confusable:

  transit   出口       station exit plate
  menu      牛肉       inside 水煮牛肉 on a menu
  street    药店       shopfront fascia
  market    斤         the 500g trap on a price label
  safety    小心地滑   hazard board

WHAT CHANGED: the breakdown is no longer a footnote on the outcome card. It is now the body of the reveal, and nothing advances it but a tap.

The evidence forced this. A path analysis of 252 international students learning Chinese found morphological awareness — knowing that words come apart into meaning-bearing pieces — is the largest single contributor to L2 Chinese reading, ahead of vocabulary size and well ahead of working memory. That makes this screen the one that actually teaches, so it gets the room.

The promoted surface at full height.

FIVE BEATS:

1. The word, on the same light ground the sign used — what you just read is what you now study.

2. IT COMES APART. 牛 ox + 肉 meat. Chinese has no separate word for beef; it names the animal and the substance and lets you do the arithmetic.

3. THE SAME MOVE AGAIN. Swap the head: 猪肉 pork, 羊肉 lamb, 鸡肉 chicken, 鸭肉 duck.

4. CAN YOU SEE THE ANIMAL? Three of them are real pictographs — 牛 is an ox head seen head-on, 羊 the same head with the horns curving down, 鱼 a head-body-tail fish. The rest are not, and the panel says so: 鸭 is 甲 (sound only) + 鸟 (bird), and 猪 has no pig in it at all — 犭 is just "four-legged animal" — though the traditional 豬 keeps one in 豕.

   This beat is where the product is most tempted to lie. Chineasy's documented failure is presenting invented pictographic stories as etymology; it delights, and it teaches confident misreading. The truthful account is also the more useful one — 鸟 means bird wherever it appears, so it opens 鸡 鸭 鹅 鸽 at once, while a made-up duck opens one character.

5. THE UNLOCK. 肉 flattens into 月 on the left, and the organ section stops being a lottery: 肝 liver, 肠 intestine, 肚 tripe, 腰 kidney, 脑 brain.

NOT SHIPPED AS SHOWN: this artboard stacks two unlocks so both can be judged. The app shows one per reveal — the coherence principle warns against piling on extra interesting material, and this is already the longest screen in the game.

The five treatments side by side.

Each caption says what the object is and what makes it hard — the shopfront is deliberately the least legible, the price label deliberately buries the character under the price, because those are the real reading conditions.

What this costs: five sign templates instead of one, and every new category needs a treatment designed for it rather than a colour picked for it.

Still open, pending the research: whether tone colour survives the evidence, and whether the gloss should be Dutch or English (both shown for now).
